pictures.scene: Edouard Brandon, Scene in a Synagogue — a dim synagogue where a bearded man in a pale fringed prayer shawl carries the Torah scroll in its tall silver case up the carpeted steps while elders in black hats, a boy holding candles and families of worshippers watch from behind the carved wooden rail, then some pharisees and scribes came to jesus from jerusalem and asked, why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders, they do not wash their hands before they eat, jesus replied, and why do you break the command of god for the sake of your tradition
pictures.name: pd_brandon_scene_in_a_synagogue

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses with the Ten Commandments — the white bearded lawgiver in a blue mantle over a gold embroidered robe, two rays of light rising from his head, holding up the stone tablet whose fourth line commands a man to honor his father and his mother, for god said, honor your father and mother and anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death, but you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to god
pictures.name: pd_champaigne_moses_with_the_ten_commandments

pictures.scene: Michelangelo, Isaiah — the seated prophet in a rose robe and green mantle, grey haired and heavy browed, turning sharply over his shoulder with one finger still keeping his place in a closed book while a red curled attendant leans at his ear, he need not honor his father or mother with it, thus you nullify the word of god for the sake of your tradition, you hypocrites, isaiah prophesied correctly about you
pictures.name: pd_michelangelo_isaiah

pictures.scene: Dirck van Delen, The Pharisee and the Publican — a tall pale church interior with a chequered marble floor where the Pharisee in a wine red robe stands beside a pillar with his face lifted and his hands spread wide, while far to the right the tax collector stands with his head bowed and both hands pressed to his breast, these people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me, they worship me in vain, they teach as doctrine the precepts of men
pictures.name: pd_delen_pharisee_and_publican

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — the apostle standing on a low step in a rose mantle over a green tunic with both hands raised and a faint halo behind his head, the Athenians seated and standing close around him under heavy stone arches, jesus called the crowd to him and said, listen and understand, a man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Jean Francois Millet, Man with a Hoe — a labourer in a loose white shirt, heavy blue trousers and wooden clogs leaning worn out on the handle of his hoe over broken stony ground where uprooted thistles lie scattered, a hazy plain and the smoke of burning weeds behind him, then the disciples came to him and said, are you aware that the pharisees were offended when they heard this, but jesus replied, every plant that my heavenly father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots
pictures.name: pd_millet_man_with_a_hoe

pictures.scene: David Teniers the Younger, The Blind Leading the Blind — a blind beggar in a brown coat with a staff and a pewter tankard stumbling forward while a boy tugs him on by the belt and a small child trots beside them, another man already tumbling backwards into the ditch at the right, a shepherd and his sheep in the field beyond, disregard them, they are blind guides, if a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit, peter said to him, explain this parable to us
pictures.name: pd_teniers_the_blind_leading_the_blind

pictures.scene: Diego Velazquez, An Old Woman Cooking Eggs — an old woman in a white headcloth and a russet jacket turning her head to speak while she lifts a wooden spoon over two eggs setting in a red earthenware pan on a little brazier, another egg in her hand, a brass mortar, a knife and a white bowl on the board before her, do you still not understand, jesus asked, do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_an_old_woman_cooking_eggs

pictures.scene: Adriaen Brouwer, Peasant Brawl — angry villagers outside a tavern where a man in yellow hose and a black hat is dragged back at the left and a woman in a white kerchief and red skirt throws herself on a man who has drawn a long knife, jugs and a mug knocked about a trestle, a pig rooting at the right and a ruined tower beyond, but the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man, for out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander
pictures.name: pd_brouwer_peasant_brawl

pictures.scene: Gustav Bauernfeind, Gate in Jerusalem — a sunlit stone street running out under a tall pointed arch with latticed oriel windows above it, people in eastern robes and headcloths filing through the shaded bazaar, a boy in a red vest walking a dog, an old man leaning on a staff and traders resting against the wall at the right, these are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him, leaving that place, jesus withdrew to the district of tyre and sidon
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Nicolas Poussin, Ruth and Boaz — the foreign woman kneeling in the stubble with one hand stretched out in appeal, a white blouse and a blue skirt, while Boaz in a yellow mantle and a white turban stands over her and points her toward his own field, reapers bending to the barley behind and a hill town under a stormy sky, and a canaanite woman from that region came to him, crying out, lord, son of david, have mercy on me, my daughter is miserably possessed by a demon, but jesus did not answer a word, so his disciples came and urged him, send her away, for she keeps crying out after us
pictures.name: pd_poussin_ruth_and_boaz

pictures.scene: Bernhard Plockhorst, The Good Shepherd — Christ walking barefoot on a stony path in a deep red robe and a pale mantle, a golden halo behind his head and a shepherd's staff in his left hand, carrying a found lamb against his breast while the rest of the flock presses in on either side, he answered, i was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of israel, the woman came and knelt before him, lord, help me, she said
pictures.name: pd_plockhorst_the_good_shepherd

pictures.scene: Nicolaes Maes, Old Woman Saying Grace — an old woman in a white cap and red sleeves sitting alone with her eyes closed and her hands folded over a laid table, a loaf of bread, a plate of fish, a small bowl and an earthenware jug set out before her on the white cloth, but jesus replied, it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs, yes, lord, she said, even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table
pictures.name: pd_maes_old_woman_saying_grace

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — a man in a dark green coat standing with his back to us on a rocky summit, a cane in his hand and his fair hair lifted by the wind, looking out over ridges and crags that rise out of a white sea of cloud, o woman, jesus answered, your faith is great, let it be done for you as you desire, and her daughter was healed from that very hour, moving on from there, jesus went along the sea of galilee, then he went up on a mountain and sat down
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Healing the Blind — Christ in a rose tunic and a billowing blue mantle bending his head and reaching down to touch the eyes of a blind man at the edge of the frame, a long colonnaded piazza opening behind him and two figures in yellow and rose crouched together on the paving at the right, large crowds came to him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and laid them at his feet, and he healed them, the crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing, and they glorified the god of israel
pictures.name: pd_elgreco_healing_the_blind

pictures.scene: Carl Haag, Danger in the Desert — a bedouin in a heavy striped cloak and a fringed headcloth standing with his lance beside his couched and loaded camel, looking out across a bare yellow waste that runs flat to the horizon with nothing on it, then jesus called his disciples to him and said, i have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with me three days and have nothing to eat, i do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way, the disciples replied, where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd
pictures.name: pd_haag_danger_in_the_desert

pictures.scene: Raphael, The Miraculous Draught of Fishes — Christ seated in the stern of a low boat in a blue tunic and a white mantle with his hand raised in blessing, Peter kneeling before him with both palms lifted and another fisherman leaning in from the next boat, the planks between them heaped with the silver catch and birds wheeling over the lake, how many loaves do you have, jesus asked, seven, they replied, and a few small fish, and he instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground
pictures.name: pd_raphael_draught_of_fishes

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, Prayer before the Meal — a bare Dutch room where a mother in a white cap holds her baby on her knee and the father and a child bow their heads with folded hands over the table, a round loaf and a cheese on the white cloth, a joint of meat on a pewter dish set on a barrel and a written verse pinned to the wall above them, taking the seven loaves and the fish, he gave thanks and broke them, then he gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people, they all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Claude Lorrain, Seaport with the Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba — a calm harbour at sunrise with the low sun laying a path of light across the water, tall ships riding at anchor on either side with their sails half furled, a rowing boat full of oarsmen pulling out from the quay and a fortified mole closing the bay beyond, a total of four thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children, after jesus had dismissed the crowds, he got into the boat and went to the region of magadan
pictures.name: pd_claude_lorrain_seaport_with_the_embarkation_of_the_queen_of_sheba

lines.text: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked, Why do Your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before they eat.
Jesus replied, And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
For God said, Honor your father and mother and Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.
But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,
he need not honor his father or mother with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you:
These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.
Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, Listen and understand.
A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.
Then the disciples came to Him and said, Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?
But Jesus replied, Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.
Disregard them! They are blind guides. If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.
Peter said to Him, Explain this parable to us.
Do you still not understand? Jesus asked.
Do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?
But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.
Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that region came to Him, crying out, Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.
But Jesus did not answer a word. So His disciples came and urged Him, Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.
He answered, I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
The woman came and knelt before Him. Lord, help me! she said.
But Jesus replied, It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs.
Yes, Lord, she said, even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table.
O woman, Jesus answered, your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire. And her daughter was healed from that very hour.
Moving on from there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee. Then He went up on a mountain and sat down.
Large crowds came to Him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and laid them at His feet, and He healed them.
The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way.
The disciples replied, Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?
How many loaves do you have? Jesus asked. Seven, they replied, and a few small fish.
And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
A total of four thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children.
After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
